newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Martinair relocates freighter to Miami.
newsitem.headline: Martinair relocates freighter to Miami.

text.p: Martinair Holland NV, the airfreight to passenger charter airline, has relocated one of its MD-11 freighter aircraft on a semi-permanent basis to Miami.
A spokesman for the airline, jointly owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV and Nedlloyd said the move reflects increasing freight business it has secured throughout South America.

"We fly from Miami to a variety of destinations in Latin America, and the aircraft flies ex-Miami to Buenos Aires two times weekly, to Bogata three times a week, and to Lima, Mexico City and Santiago once a week," Martinair's spokesman told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Martinair rotates the Miami-based aircraft with a second aircraft on a regular basis, giving it the opportunity to return its MD-11 to Amsterdam, where the airline's service centre is located.

"The decision to locate an aircraft in the U.S. reflects the very fast development of the South and Latin American airfreght markets." Sales for the aircraft are handled by Martinair Americas, its Miami-based sales and marketing wing, the spokesman said..

At the start of November, Martinair said it was buying a 40 percent stake in Colombian airline company Tampa and a 10 percent share in Florida-based Martin Aviation Group (MAG), a cargo sales and services representative for South America. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
